content:
InfraBot: [ALERT] 4xx/5xx spike from API gateway - spike started 2026-03-15T09:02Z. Detected elevated TLS handshake failures (525/522) across multiple Cloudflare POPs. Paging oncall.
Ajay: saw it, getting the oncall now. region: eu-west looks worst.
Marta: I'm on phone but mobilizing. @Samir are you available to take first pass? I can do customer comms.
Samir: taking it — oncall handoff. thanks. starting checklist: 1) confirm scope 2) check CF status 3) gather logs 4) mitigation.
Leo: adding context — we have internal observability alerts for TLS errors and increased retry latency. Some customers reporting timeouts to /v1/generate.
Samir: quick checks — Cloudflare status page shows intermittent "performance issues" note for Europe but no detailed incident: https://www.cloudflarestatus.com/ (linking)
Samir: running curl from eu instance:
```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.internal/health
* Connected to api.redwood-inference.edge (1.2.3.4) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake: SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to api...:443
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca
```
Samir: our edge logs show repeated 525 responses from Cloudflare. snippet:
```
2026-03-15T09:03:12Z INF request_id=abc123 route=/v1/generate client=198.51.100.12 cf_pop=AMS
response_code=525 cf_ray=abcd1234 tls_failure=1
```
Marta: CS-Bot ping — are any paying customers in EU experiencing large-scale failures? we need to segment impact.
CS-Bot: Customer pings: three mid-market customers in EU reporting 50-80% failed requests since 09:00Z. No major enterprise-wide PagerDuty escalations yet.
Samir: rolling through our routing/edge metrics — pathing shows increased failures for CF POPs: AMS, FRA, LHR. US POPs fine.
Leo: can we flip to a fallback region or origin bypass for affected customers? what's the fallback route in the runbook?
Samir: runbook excerpt: 1) increase origin retries (short-term) 2) route EU traffic to alternate POPs (if CF supports steering) 3) if severe, failover to direct origin endpoint (bypass CF) — requires auth header rotation and firewall ACL tweak.
Sylvia: direct origin bypass is high-risk but doable. We have a pre-validated origin endpoint: https://direct-origin.internal:8443. It requires token X-Direct: <rotating-token>. Ops runbook has token rotation script.
Marta: I prefer steering first, then bypass only if customers still impacted. Updating CS to tell customers we're investigating and we may enable a temporary bypass.
Ajay: Samir, can you open a Cloudflare support ticket? include sample cf_ray, timestamps, and example request ids. escalate to P1 if they have internal outages.
Samir: opened ticket REF-20260315-7890 and requested urgent investigation. pasted logs and cf_rays.
Samir: mitigation attempt 1: increased retries from 2->5 for EU routes via runtime config. pushed canary to 10% traffic to test.
Leo: can we also reduce request timeouts to avoid long client waits? or will that exacerbate failures? concerned about increased QPS.
Samir: reduced client timeout from 10s -> 5s for retry loop, so we fail fast and let retries kick in. canary metrics look slightly better at 10%.
Marta: CS message draft: "We're investigating increased TLS handshake failures to our EU edge. We're working with Cloudflare and may enable temporary routing changes to maintain availability. We'll update in 30 minutes." approve?
Ajay: approve. send.
Marta: sent to affected customers. added note for status page.
Samir: CF support replied: "We're seeing degraded TLS handshakes at several POPs due to an internal cert chain update. Engineers investigating. Temporary mitigation: avoid affected POPs or use direct origin if necessary." (quoting)
Leo: ok, that confirms root cause likely CF-side. What's our plan of record?
Samir: plan: 1) increase retries universally for EU 2) widen canary from 10->50% if no regression 3) if still failing, coordinate with infra to enable direct-origin bypass for highest-impact customers 4) keep CS messages every 30 min and update status page.
Sylvia: I'll start prepping the firewall ACL change for direct-origin bypass and pre-generate tokens. don't flip without Ajay or Marta signoff.
Ajay: agreed. we need approval from security for token use — pinging @Sylvia for security checklist.
Sylvia: security checklist done in parallel: short TTL tokens, single-use rotations, audit logs on.
Marta: timeline update: 09:18Z — CF reports investigating; retries and canary in place; customer impact reduced for 30% of requests but some still fail.
CS-Bot: Notifying SLAs team for impacted customers for tracking.
Samir: at 09:35Z we expanded canary to 50%. EU error rate dropped from 18% -> 6% on the canary segment.
Leo: good. should we scale up worker pools to handle extra retry load? increased retries means more tokens consumed.
Samir: scaling up by 20% for EU autoscaling group as precaution.
Marta: customer comms 09:45Z: "Partial mitigation in place; Cloudflare continues investigation. If you see issues, please DM support." Received 2 follow-ups, one complaining about degraded latency.
Ajay: keep an eye on billing impact from retries/extra throughput — flag to FinOps after incident.
Samir: 10:05Z CF: "Root cause identified: cert chain propagation issue affecting select POPs. Fix rolling out. Expected full remediation in ~30-60 minutes."
Marta: prepping postmortem and communication to customers with timeline and mitigations we used.
Sylvia: after fix begins, monitor for TLS handshake metrics returning to baseline. will rollback retries and autoscaling after stable 1 hour.
Samir: 10:48Z — CF confirms fix complete. Observability: EU TLS failures back to baseline; overall 5xx down to normal.
Marta: closing loop: CS updated customers and marked incident as "mitigated - external dependency (Cloudflare)". We'll run a post-incident retro and action items.
Ajay: key action items: 1) validate direct-origin bypass automation and docs 2) add a playbook for Cloudflare cert-chain issues 3) update alert thresholds to detect POP-localized TLS flaps faster.
Samir: will create incident ticket and attach logs + CF support correspondence. REF-20260315-7890 -> linked.
Marta: nice work everyone. filing postmortem draft and scheduling 1hr retro.
InfraBot: Incident closed (mitigated) at 2026-03-15T10:48Z.
